raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`Glm47MoeDetector.parse_streaming_increment` (parsers `glm47` and `iquest_q1`) runs `re.search(r"<tool_call>(.*?)(?:(<arg_key.*?))?(?:(</tool_call>)|$)", ...)` over the whole buffered tool call on every streamed chunk. The lazy groups make the regex engine step through the buffer one character at a time, so a long call (a file write, say) costs quadratic time on the tokenizer manager's event loop. A 64 KB argument took about 7 s of CPU for one request.

## Modifications

- `_match_partial_tool_call` finds the same spans with `str.find`: the first `<tool_call>`, then whichever of `<arg_key` or `</tool_call>` comes first. It returns the same stripped name, stripped arguments, end marker and match end the regex groups gave, and replaces the regex and `_extract_match_groups`.
- Two tests: one checks the helper against the old regex on every prefix of some tricky inputs, the other streams a long value containing tag-like text in 3-char chunks.

## Accuracy Tests

Parser-only change, model output is untouched. I ran a differential test of the old and new detectors (`Glm47MoeDetector` and `IQuestQ1Detector`) on 108k random inputs mixing well-formed calls and tag soup, random chunking and 6 argument types. Every chunk's normal_text and calls, plus `finish()` and the final state, matched exactly. The helper also matched the regex on about 2.7M prefixes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One write_file call streamed token by token with the GLM-4.5-Air tokenizer, CPU only, median of 7 alternating fresh processes per side:

| Content | Deltas | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 KB | 480 | 10.5 ms | 2.4 ms | 4.4x |
| 8 KB | 1885 | 136.6 ms | 12.5 ms | 10.9x |
| 25 KB | 4737 | 896.5 ms | 57.1 ms | 15.7x |
| 64 KB | 13086 | 6988 ms | 323 ms | 21.6x |

Before, 97% of the parse time was in `re.Pattern.search`; afterwards the profile is flat.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

-    def _extract_match_groups(self, match: re.Match) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
-        """Extract function name, arguments and end marker from regex match.
+    def _match_partial_tool_call(
+        self, text: str
+    ) -> Optional[tuple[str, str, str, int]]:
+        """Match the first, possibly unfinished, tool call in a streaming buffer.
 
-        Args:
-            match: Regex match object
+        Same result as searching for
+        ``<tool_call>(.*?)(?:(<arg_key.*?))?(?:(</tool_call>)|$)`` (DOTALL),
+        but with ``str.find``: the lazy regex walks the whole buffer one
+        character at a time on every streamed chunk.
 
         Returns:
-            (func_name, func_args_raw, is_tool_end)
+            (func_name, func_args_raw, is_tool_end, match_end), or None. ``match_end``
+            is the index after the end token, or -1 while the call is unfinished.
         """
-        func_name = match.group(1).strip()
-        func_args_raw = match.group(2).strip() if match.group(2) else ""
-        is_tool_end = match.group(3) or ""
-        return func_name, func_args_raw, is_tool_end
+        start = text.find(self.bot_token)
+        if start == -1:
+            return None
+        name_start = start + len(self.bot_token)
+        arg_start = text.find("<arg_key", name_start)
+        end_start = text.find(self.eot_token, name_start)
+        call_end = end_start if end_start != -1 else len(text)
+        if arg_start != -1 and arg_start < call_end:
+            name_end = arg_start
+            func_args_raw = text[arg_start:call_end].strip()
+        else:
+            name_end = call_end
+            func_args_raw = ""
+
+        func_name = text[name_start:name_end].strip()
+        if end_start == -1:
+            return func_name, func_args_raw, "", -1
+        return func_name, func_args_raw, self.eot_token, end_start + len(self.eot_token)

 import functools
 import json
+import re
 import unittest
 import warnings
 
@@ -3694,6 +3695,53 @@ def test_required_tool_choice_falls_back_when_native_tag_is_unavailable(self):
             self.assertEqual("json_schema", constraint[0])
             _glm47_native_structural_tag_available.cache_clear()
 
+    def test_streaming_partial_match_same_as_regex(self):
+        # _match_partial_tool_call replaced this regex search on every chunk.
+        pattern = re.compile(
+            r"<tool_call>(.*?)(?:(<arg_key.*?))?(?:(</tool_call>)|$)", re.DOTALL
+        )
+        texts = [
+            "<tool_call>get_weather<arg_key>city</arg_key>"
+            "<arg_value>a < b </tool_ \n</arg_value></tool_call>\n",
+            "Sure.<tool_call> get_weather \n</tool_call><tool_call>x<arg_key",
+            "<tool_call>f</tool_call><arg_key>k</arg_key></tool_call>",
+            "<tool_call>f<arg_k\n<arg_key>k</arg_key>\n",
+        ]
+        for text in texts:
+            for end in range(len(text) + 1):
+                prefix = text[:end]
+                with self.subTest(prefix=prefix):
+                    m = pattern.search(prefix)
+                    expected = m and (
+                        m.group(1).strip(),
+                        m.group(2).strip() if m.group(2) else "",
+                        m.group(3) or "",
+                        m.end() if m.group(3) else -1,
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        self.detector._match_partial_tool_call(prefix), expected
+                    )
+
+    def test_streaming_long_value_with_tag_like_text(self):
+        value = "if a < b: print('</arg_ <tool_call> <arg_k')\n" * 200
+        text = (
+            "<tool_call>get_weather<arg_key>city</arg_key>"
+            f"<arg_value>{value}</arg_value>"
+            "<arg_key>date</arg_key><arg_value>2024-06-27</arg_value></tool_call>"
+        )
+        calls = []
+        for i in range(0, len(text), 3):
+            calls.extend(
+                self.detector.parse_streaming_increment(
+                    text[i : i + 3], self.tools
+                ).calls
+            )
+        self.assertEqual(calls[0].name, "get_weather")
+        self.assertEqual(
+            json.loads("".join(call.parameters for call in calls)),
+            {"city": value, "date": "2024-06-27"},
+        )
+
